extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, campus administrators, and legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for institutions to adopt, publish, and implement Title IX grievance procedures that promptly and equitably resolve sex discrimination and sex-based harassment complaints, including additional protections for postsecondary students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline standards for grievance procedures (§106.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must set baseline standards to ensure a fair process under Title IX, including the equitable treatment of the parties; decisionmakers who are free of bias or conflicts of interest; adequate notice to the parties of the allegations and timeframes for grievance procedures; guidelines for ensuring the adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation of the complaint; the opportunity for parties to present evidence; and guidelines for how a decisionmaker must assess such evidence and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department anticipates many recipients already have similar protections; where final regulatory requirements exceed existing procedures, the benefits justify any burden. Recipients may implement these baseline standards within existing procedures so long as they do not conflict with §§106.45/106.46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures must be in writing (§106.45(a)(1) and §106.46(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures are required to be in writing so that recipients and participants are informed of obligations and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must adopt, publish, and implement written grievance procedures and nondiscrimination policies (see §106.8(b)(2)). Written procedures help ensure clarity about prompt and equitable resolution and participants’ rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must provide for the prompt resolution of sex discrimination complaints; Title IX's regulations have required promptness in grievance procedures since 1975.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary delay; prompt resolution furthers Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate and is balanced against needs for thorough, equitable processes in different educational settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment (equal treatment does not require identical treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must ensure equitable treatment of parties; equal treatment does not require identical treatment and procedures may recognize distinct rights (e.g., employee contractual rights) while still satisfying baseline requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may adopt provisions that apply equally to the parties (§106.45(j)); they may account for different statuses (employee vs non-employee) provided the baseline requirements are met and applied equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to employees and students (Title IX scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX applies to all sex discrimination occurring in a recipient's education program or activity regardless of whether the parties are students, employees, or third parties; employees covered by Title IX should be afforded prompt and equitable grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An employee's position, tenure, part-time, or at-will status should not dictate whether the employee is subject to procedural protections under these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with Title VII, state law, and collective bargaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may need to comply with both Title VII and Title IX, and with applicable State/local law and collective bargaining agreements; contractual arrangements must conform to Federal law as a condition of receiving Federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should attempt to implement grievance procedures that function alongside Title VII and other laws. If a conflict arises, the recipient must fulfill Title IX obligations (§106.6(b)). The Department will not require union consultation, but recipients may consult unions voluntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing processes and collective bargaining procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations prohibits a recipient from using an existing process (e.g., grievance procedures in a collective bargaining agreement) to satisfy the requirements of §§106.45 or 106.46 as long as those procedures do not conflict with the requirements of these sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using an existing single procedure that meets Title IX requirements can avoid multiple proceedings and delay. However, if an employee elects a collective bargaining remedy that does not include the baseline requirements consistent with §106.45 (and if applicable §106.46), there can be no Title IX finding of responsibility or Title IX disciplinary action against that respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.46: Additional procedures for postsecondary student-involved sex-based harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: For postsecondary institutions, §106.46 establishes additional requirements for sex-based harassment complaints involving a student complainant or respondent (only applies when a postsecondary student is a complainant or respondent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These additional protections include written notice of allegations (§106.46(c)); providing parties the same opportunity, if any, to have persons other than their advisor present (§106.46(e)(3)); recipient discretion to allow or limit expert witnesses (§106.46(e)(4)); making live hearings and cross‑examination by a party's advisor discretionary (§106.46(f) and (g)); allowing parties to be accompanied by an advisor (§106.46(e)(2)); equal opportunity to access relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence (§106.46(e)(6)); and opportunities to appeal dismissals or determinations (§106.46(i)). These measures are intended to mitigate power imbalances and be age‑ and context‑appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator/decisionmaker impartiality and bias protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers and investigators must be free of bias or conflicts of interest and the grievance procedures must include safeguards to ensure adequate, reliable, and impartial investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training requirements (§106.8(d)) support impartiality; recipients must ensure those performing Title IX roles receive appropriate training related to their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice, opportunity to present evidence, and evidence assessment guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must provide adequate notice to parties of allegations and timeframes; give parties the opportunity to present evidence; and include guidelines for how decisionmakers should assess evidence and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should describe timelines, what constitutes admissible evidence, how credibility will be evaluated, and ensure both parties have fair access to information used in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures and mitigation of power imbalances
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer and coordinate supportive measures (per §106.44(g)) as appropriate to support complainants and mitigate power imbalances that could chill reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures plus training help create conditions that enable reporting and fair participation in grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must determine whether to initiate a sex discrimination complaint consistent with §106.44(f)(1)(v) and must take prompt and effective steps to address sex discrimination under §106.44(f)(1)(vii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator obligations remain even if an employee pursues remedies under a collective bargaining agreement; the Coordinator must make fact‑specific determinations about initiation and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal rule for non-participating respondents (§106.45(d)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss a complaint when the respondent is not participating in the recipient's education program or activity and is not employed by the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dismissal provision is incorporated into §106.46(a) and governs when a recipient may decline to proceed under Title IX grievance procedures for non-participating/non-employed respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural protections before disciplinary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must require certain measures before imposing disciplinary sanctions (including termination or suspension) to ensure sanctions themselves are not applied in a way that discriminates on the basis of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures are part of ensuring nondiscriminatory treatment of both complainants and respondents and help prevent arbitrary or disparate application of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to tailor procedures by educational level and context
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations provide baseline requirements but allow recipients flexibility to tailor procedures to different educational settings (elementary, secondary, postsecondary) and contexts while maintaining promptness and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.46 adds postsecondary‑specific safeguards recognizing students’ age/maturity and potential power differentials; §106.45 provides baseline protections appropriate across settings. Recipients may solicit public input voluntarily but are not required by Title IX to hold public hearings prior to adoption.
